You are a data-extraction subagent for the research agent "claude". claude is building an in-house 3D MHD solar-wind model and must benchmark it against a CCMC Runs-on-Request ENLIL simulation that an external reviewer recommended: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/ror/results/viewrun.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1 (ENLIL 2.8f, WSA 5.4/GONGz time-dependent boundary, 64 cone CMEs, grid 576x24x90, 0.1–3.1 AU, ±48° latitude, output 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-09 every 6 h, HEEQ+180 frame). The run page offers virtual-spacecraft timeseries: "View ENLIL at 3I-Atlas / earth / stereoa / solo / mars / parkersp / venus / mercury / juice / psyche". These link to /cgi-bin/visualizers/idl1d/run_idl1d.cgi?dir=47767&file=ENLIL_at_3I-Atlas.txt (and similarly for the others). The run also has "Browse individual output files" (/ror/results/run_files.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1), "Request output data in bulk" (/ror/results/request_output.php?runnumber=...), "Download output .dat files", and a 3D viewer (/cgi-bin/visualizers/vis3d/CCMCVis_3D.cgi?dir=47767). Saved copies of the run page and of the 1D-viewer page are in mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/ (viewrun.html, idl1d_3i.html, post_3i.html). Work fully autonomously: no human will answer questions.

WORKSPACE (write only here): /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/ (put the timeseries in ref/ccmc/timeseries/, images in ref/ccmc/quicklook/, scripts in ref/ccmc/scripts/). Never write elsewhere, especially not in mhd_llm/argon, mhd_llm/codex, or mhd_llm/shared_notes.

KNOWN BEHAVIOR: the CCMC server intermittently returns "500 Proxy Error ... SSL Handshake" pages (about 270 bytes). Retry with backoff (for example 10 tries, 5–20 s apart), and always check the size and content of every response. The 1D-viewer form POSTs to the same CGI URL with fields debug=0, dir=47767, file=ENLIL_at_3I-Atlas.txt, UseMJD=1, Time0, Time1 (days since run start, range 0.000469041–69.0006), Quantity1/2/3 (indices into: R Lat Lon V_r V_lon V_lat B_r B_lon B_lat N T E_r E_lon E_lat V B P_ram BP E P ExB_r ExB_lat ExB_lon ExB NV_r NV_lat NV_lon NV, starting at 0), PlotMagni, linestyle, psym, symsize, and Output_Pointdata=1 ("Have data printed to text file"). One POST I tried returned a link /idl_images/pointdata_<id>.txt reported as "0.00 KB" whose URL returned an HTML page, so you need to find the request that actually produces the data: perhaps with Quantity choices that include N, V_r, and T, or after the plot is generated, or via a GET. Also try to find the raw ENLIL_at_*.txt files directly, e.g. under https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/RoR_WWW/SH/ENLIL/2025/Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1/ or paths revealed by run_files.php. Read the page HTML/JS to discover the real file locations. Do not download the 46 GB 3D output. Small 2D/ecliptic products or a handful of 3D time slices (each under ~200 MB, total under 1.5 GB) are fine if they are easily available. Priority is the 3D slices near 2025-11-25, 2025-11-30, 2025-12-03 and 2025-12-04, in whatever format the server provides (ENLIL tim.*.nc files would be ideal).

TASKS
1. Obtain the ENLIL virtual-spacecraft timeseries at 3I-Atlas (top priority), earth, stereoa, solo, mars, parkersp, psyche, juice, venus, mercury, with all available columns (at least time, R, Lat, Lon, V_r, N, T, B_r, B_lon, B_lat, and ideally V_lon, V_lat). Save the raw responses and tidy CSVs: ref/ccmc/timeseries/enlil_<body>.csv with columns utc (ISO), r_au, lat_deg, lon_deg, vr_kms, vlon_kms, vlat_kms, n_cm3, T_K, br_nT, blon_nT, blat_nT (whatever exists), with units verified from headers. Document the time convention (days since 2025-10-01T00 and so on) and the coordinate system of Lat/Lon.
2. Download the quick-look animations or frames (den3-earth_low3syn, vel3-earth_low3syn, ...) into ref/ccmc/quicklook/ for qualitative comparison.
3. If any 3D or 2D field data for specific times are obtainable at a modest size, fetch those near 2025-12-03/04 and document the format.
4. QC: plot ref/ccmc/qc_enlil_3i.png showing ENLIL n, V_r, n*V_r (cm^-2 s^-1), and T at 3I-Atlas over 2025-11-15 to 2025-12-09, with the XMM window 2025-12-03T12:04–2025-12-04T10:12 shaded. Make a similar plot for earth and stereoa.
5. Write ref/ccmc/README.md describing what you obtained, how (exact URLs and requests), formats, and units.
Python: /home/scabot/miniconda3/bin/python3 (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, astropy). Use at most 2 CPU threads and 2 GB RAM. CODE STYLE: minimal, with no comments and no docstrings, and no free-text note fields in output JSON or CSV. American spelling.

FINAL REPLY (compact): files obtained and their columns and units; summary numbers for ENLIL at 3I-Atlas during the XMM window (median and min/max of n, V_r, n·V_r, and T), and at Earth and STEREO-A over Nov 20–Dec 5 (medians); whether any 3D data was retrieved; and the exact working request recipe.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>
